description: An upstream rate-limit reply (429 with retry-after) reaches the client as a 429 with the Claude error envelope and the upstream's error type and message. Today's core answers with its own Retry-After, which changes from run to run (its cooldown estimate), so the header is masked here; the Chat 429 cases pin that the new core passes on the upstream's value.

error.message: Number of request tokens has exceeded your per-minute rate limit
Number of request tokens has exceeded your per-minute rate limit

headers.Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, X-Api-Key, X-Goog-Api-Key, Anthropic-Version, Anthropic-Beta
headers.Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
headers.Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-CPA-TRACE-ID, X-CPA-VERSION, X-CPA-COMMIT, X-CPA-BUILD-DATE, X-CPA-SUPPORT-PLUGIN, X-CPA-HOME-VERSION, X-CPA-HOME-BUILD-DATE, X-SERVER-VERSION, X-SERVER-BUILD-DATE, Location, Retry-After, ETag, X-Request-Id, OpenAI-Request-Id

exceptions.reason: Today's core reaches a Messages upstream only through its Claude API-key provider, which rewrites the request even for a custom base URL: it adds cache_control breakpoints, removes the thinking setting and thinking blocks whose signatures it cannot verify, drops a cache TTL, adds stream false, adds ?beta=true and sends the key as a bearer token with its own Accept and Accept-Encoding. The new core passes a Messages request to a Messages upstream unchanged, thinking blocks, signatures and cache_control included, and sends the key in x-api-key as Anthropic's API defines; Claude-specific rewrites belong to the Claude provider extension (slice 10).
